verdict.rationale: Blaxel's docs say sandboxes keep their state in standby and resume in under 25ms "even after weeks" ([blaxel-docs-2], [blaxel-docs-16]). Expiration policies based on TTL or inactivity let you control how long a sandbox persists ([blaxel-docs-25]). Archive/unarchive, snapshots and volumes preserve state across very long tasks ([blaxel-docs-22], [blaxel-docs-21], [blaxel-docs-29]). The caveat is that sandboxes scale to zero after about 5s of inactivity, so long sessions are kept alive mainly by standby and resume rather than by documented continuous compute. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of maximum continuous runtime or whether active processes keep a sandbox awake for hours or days, and independent or hands-on corroboration of multi-day sessions.
